summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 20.3 to Angular 21.2 (and @ngrx/* to 21.1.1 for the peer range, typescript to 5.9.3). The core migrations added `provideZoneChangeDetection()` to the bootstrap call (v21 makes zoneless the default, so this preserves current behaviour) and rewrote the three templates that used `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` to built-in control flow. The webpack `browser`/`server` builders are still shipped in @angular-devkit/build-angular 21, so the project keeps them and `npm run build` / `npm run build:ssr` both pass; tests still fail exactly as at baseline.
changes: `ng update @angular/core@21 @angular/cli@21` rewrote package.json (all @angular/* to 21.2.25, @angular/cli and @angular-devkit/build-angular to 21.2.28, typescript to ~5.9.3) but its own install step failed, so the install and the migrations were finished by hand (see below).

Install needed a one-time clean regeneration: the half-updated node_modules/package-lock left npm with an unsolvable tree (ERESOLVE on @angular-devkit/build-angular, then an npm 'Cannot read properties of null (reading edgesOut)' crash). Removing node_modules + package-lock.json and running `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` once produced a working lockfile; after that a plain `npm install` on a deleted node_modules succeeds (exit 0), which is what the checks use.

Bumped the five @ngrx/* packages from 20.1.0 to 21.1.1. Required: @ngrx 20 peers on `@angular/core: ^20.0.0`. @ngrx ships no 19/20/21 migrations (newest on disk are the 18_0_0-beta ones for store and effects), so nothing was skipped.

Ran the @angular/core v21 migrations with `ng update @angular/core --migrate-only --from=20.3.34 --to=21.2.25`: 'Migrates deprecated bootstrap options to providers' changed src/main.ts to `bootstrapModule(AppModule, { applicationProviders: [provideZoneChangeDetection()] })`. Angular 21 no longer enables ZoneJS change detection implicitly, so this keeps the app's existing zone-based behaviour; zone.js stays a dependency.

The same run applied 'Converts the entire application to block control flow syntax' (no longer optional in v21), rewriting add-employee.component.html, fetch-employee.component.html and fetch-data.component.html from `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` to `@if`/`@for`. Reviewed the diff: pure structural rewrite, `@for` tracks the loop item, no `*ngIf`/`*ngFor`/`*ngSwitch` left in src.

The BootstrapContext, ApplicationConfig-import-move and Router.lastSuccessfulNavigation core migrations all reported no changes; the optional router-current-navigation migration was declined again (the app never calls Router.getCurrentNavigation).

The @angular/cli migration runner could not execute the v21 CLI migrations: `ng update` insists on downloading a temporary 'latest' CLI, and that newer CLI reports "Cannot find migration '<name>' in '@angular/cli'" for all of use-application-builder / remove-default-karma-config / update-typescript-lib / update-module-resolution. Each was therefore evaluated by hand against the migration collection in node_modules/@schematics/angular/migrations/migration-collection.json.

Applied the update-typescript-lib migration by hand: tsconfig.json `lib` is now ["es2022", "dom"] instead of ["es2017", "dom"]. update-module-resolution was already satisfied (`moduleResolution: "bundler"` since the v20 hop).

Skipped remove-default-karma-config: src/karma.conf.js is not the default content (custom base path, coverage-istanbul reporter, jasmine-html reporter), so the migration would not have removed it either.

Declined use-application-builder once more. It is marked optional/recommended, not mandatory, and `browser`, `browser-esbuild`, `server` and `protractor` are all still registered builders in @angular-devkit/build-angular 21.2.28 (verified in its builders.json) - both `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr` pass unchanged. Switching to the esbuild `application` builder would rework the SSR/aspnet-prerendering setup and the test target, which is beyond a behaviour-preserving hop; it stays the top follow-up.
Restored the trailing blank line on package.json that the ng update rewrite dropped.

Checks re-run from a deleted node_modules: `npm install` pass (exit 0, no --legacy-peer-deps), `npm run build` pass, `npm run build:ssr` pass, `npm run test -- --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless` fail with the same pre-existing angular.json styles.css load error as at baseline.
manual_followups: `npm run test` still fails exactly as at baseline: angular.json's test target lists "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so webpack reports a load error and karma aborts before any spec runs. One-line fix, deliberately left out of the upgrade hops - but it means no spec in this app has actually executed for the whole 8->21 migration, so fix it first and expect real failures behind it.

The app is now on Angular 21 but still uses the deprecated webpack `browser`/`server` builders, NgModule bootstrapping via platform-browser-dynamic, and zone-based change detection pinned by the new explicit `provideZoneChangeDetection()`. The coherent next step is the `use-application-builder` migration (`ng update @angular/cli --name use-application-builder`), then standalone components + `bootstrapApplication`, then dropping zone.js. Each is a behaviour-affecting project of its own.

`provideZoneChangeDetection()` in src/main.ts is the migration's compatibility shim, not a target state. Removing it opts the app into v21's zoneless change detection, which needs a real pass over the components (anything relying on implicit zone-triggered CD).

Karma is deprecated and the test stack here (karma 6.4, jasmine-core 3.10, karma-coverage-istanbul-reporter, @types/jasminewd2) is years stale. Move to the `application`-builder test target with Vitest or Web Test Runner when the builder migration happens.

@types/node is still ^12 while the toolchain runs Node 22; this is the only real peer conflict left and makes every `npm install` print a wall of 'ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency / Conflicting peer dependency: @types/node' warnings (vite and friends want ^20.19). Bumping it to ^22 should clear them, but it will surface new type errors, so it was left for a separate change.

The protractor/e2e project, tslint.json, codelyzer and tslint are all dead weight: `npm run lint` has been broken since the v13 hop (the tslint architect targets were deleted and nothing replaced them). Move to @angular-eslint and delete the tslint/codelyzer/protractor entries.

angular.json still carries a root `schematics` block added in the v20 hop purely to preserve pre-v20 generated-file naming, plus `defaultConfiguration: ""` on the build and server targets from the v12 migration. Both can go if the project adopts current defaults.
`HTTP_INTERCEPTORS` is still imported but unused in src/app/app.module.ts.
Every component still carries an explicit `standalone: false` from the v19 hop.

rxjs is still 6.6.7 (end-of-life). Angular 21 still accepts `^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0` and @ngrx 21 `^6.5.3 || ^7.5.0`, so nothing forces the move yet, but rxjs 7 should be adopted deliberately rather than at the next hop's mercy.

The SSR setup still looks like dead code: Startup.cs uses UseSpa/UseAngularCliServer and never UseSpaPrerendering, and aspnet-prerendering is a 2018-era package. Deleting the server target and aspnet-prerendering would remove most of the risk from the application-builder migration.
add-employee.component.ts still uses the Untyped* form classes from the v14 opt-out; typed reactive forms are still open.
`useDefineForClassFields: false` is still set in tsconfig.json from the v15 migration; a person should decide whether the app can move to the standard `true` behaviour.
node-sass 4.x still fails to build its native binding on modern Node and is skipped as an optional dependency; it is unused by the build and should be dropped or replaced with `sass`.
core-js is still pinned at ^2.6.5 and is almost certainly unnecessary for Angular 21's browser support; check src/polyfills.ts.
`npm install` reports 40 vulnerabilities, almost all from the stale optionalDependencies (protractor, tslint, node-sass, ts-node 5) rather than from Angular.
The Browserslist config still lists browsers outside Angular 21's support window (kaios, op_mini, and_qq, and_uc, ...), producing warnings on every build.
